note: Rebuild dlss5vk from the re-cut patch (e7bdcb5ee877, cut from odl-src commit e7bdcb5). Only src/nr_graph.cpp moved in it: routesFromEnvironment's chainMask default goes 0 -> 2, so the c32 blocks' chain is taken again while the expert chain stays off. No shader and no emitter moved, so the build must still report 17 shader modules and 78 PTX kernels - a different count means the patch did not apply cleanly, and a compile error would name src/nr_graph.cpp because that is the only file this patch touched. Quote the final stamp line: it must read port 9d08f41 at patch e7bdcb5ee877. Before this build every port run stamps OUT OF SYNC (the last landed build is patch 5c075a8a7bfb), and the two profiles queued behind this (r2026-11-10-15-gap4-1-1080p and -2-720p, their numeric prefixes sort after this one) must read the new binary - if the stamp names the old patch, do not read the profiles, report that instead. Reason for the change: the chainMask-0 pair landed and chaining's cost is size-dependent - at 2560x1440 every route without chains was cheapest (X 9.041 against T 9.436 with chainMask 0, X 9.525 against 9.397 at chainMask 2, X 10.074 against 9.380 with chaining fully on, all 249 dispatches), but at 1280x720 chains off read X 3.558 against T 3.385 where chaining fully on read X 3.277 against T 3.393, i.e. 0.281 ms cheaper chained. The shipping pass runs the network at 0.75 of the output size (1080p for a 1440p output), between the two, so the default keeps the c32 chain and the flip point is measured.
